questions.question: ABATE — synonym
questions.explanation: Abate means to become less intense. A (increase) is the opposite; C (begin) and D (conceal) are unrelated.

questions.question: LUCID — synonym
questions.explanation: Lucid means clear and easy to understand. A, B, C all describe the opposite or an unrelated quality.

questions.question: NOVICE — antonym
questions.explanation: A novice is a beginner, so the antonym is an expert. B, C, D are near-synonyms of novice.

questions.question: VIVID — synonym
questions.explanation: Vivid means bright and intense. A, B, D describe dullness or faintness.

questions.question: FRUGAL — synonym
questions.explanation: Frugal means careful with money — thrifty. A and C are opposites in spirit; D (generous) concerns giving, not saving.

questions.question: OPAQUE — antonym
questions.explanation: Opaque means not letting light through; its antonym is transparent. A, B, C are consistent with opaque.

questions.question: DILIGENT — synonym
questions.explanation: Diligent means hardworking and careful. B, C, D are opposites or unrelated.

questions.question: ADVERSE — synonym
questions.explanation: Adverse means harmful or unfavorable. A, B, D are positive terms.

questions.question: BREVITY — synonym
questions.explanation: Brevity means briefness — conciseness. A (length) is the opposite; B and C are unrelated.

questions.question: HUMBLE — antonym
questions.explanation: The antonym of humble is arrogant (proud). A, C, D are near-synonyms of humble.

questions.question: ZEAL — synonym
questions.explanation: Zeal means great enthusiasm. B (apathy) is the opposite; C and D are unrelated.

questions.question: OBSCURE — antonym
questions.explanation: The antonym of obscure (little-known, hidden) is well-known. A, B, D are near-synonyms of obscure.

questions.question: Neither the manager nor the clerks ___ present at the meeting.
questions.explanation: With "neither … nor," the verb agrees with the nearer subject ("clerks," plural) → "were."

questions.question: Each of the students ___ a laptop for the activity.
questions.explanation: "Each of the students" is singular → "has." A, C, D are plural forms.

questions.question: The committee ___ decided to postpone the hearing.
questions.explanation: "The committee" is a collective noun treated as singular here → "has." B, C, D are plural.

questions.question: Between you and ___, the plan still needs more work.
questions.explanation: After a preposition ("between"), use the object pronoun "me." A, B, D are subject pronouns.

questions.question: She is one of the employees who ___ overtime every week.
questions.explanation: The relative clause "who ___" refers to "employees" (plural), not "one" → "work." A, B, C are singular.

questions.question: If he ___ harder, he would pass the examination.
questions.explanation: Second conditional: "If he studied …, he would pass." A/C/D break the conditional pattern.

questions.question: The report, together with the annexes, ___ submitted yesterday.
questions.explanation: The subject is "The report" (singular); "together with the annexes" does not make it plural → "was."

questions.question: Which sentence uses parallel structure correctly?

options.A: She likes reading, to swim, and jogging.
options.B: She likes to read, swimming, and to jog.
options.C: She likes reading, swimming, and jogging.
options.D: She likes to read, to swim, and jogging.

questions.explanation: Parallel gerunds: "reading, swimming, and jogging." A, B, D mix gerunds and infinitives.

questions.question: Arrange in logical order: (1) Boil fresh water in a kettle. (2) Pour the hot water over the tea bag. (3) Place a tea bag in a cup. (4) Let it steep for three minutes, then remove the bag.
questions.explanation: Logical steps: boil water (1) → place tea bag (3) → pour water (2) → steep and remove (4). Only B gives this order. D is incoherent: it steeps and removes the bag (4) before any water is boiled or poured, and ends with boiling the water (1).

questions.question: Arrange in logical order: (1) Water the seedling regularly. (2) Dig a small hole in the soil. (3) Cover the roots with soil. (4) Place the seedling in the hole.
questions.explanation: Dig (2) → place seedling (4) → cover roots (3) → water (1). Only D gives this order.

questions.question: Arrange in logical order: (1) Dear Ms. Reyes, (2) I am writing to apply for the vacant clerk position. (3) Thank you for your consideration. (4) Respectfully yours, Ana Santos
questions.explanation: Letter order: greeting (1) → purpose (2) → thanks (3) → closing (4). Only A gives this order.

questions.question: Arrange in logical order: (1) Review your notes from the lesson. (2) First, choose a quiet place to study. (3) Then, set a timer for thirty minutes. (4) Finally, test yourself without looking at your notes.
questions.explanation: Choose place (2) → set timer (3) → review notes (1) → self-test (4). Only C gives this order. B is incoherent: it opens with the "Finally" self-test (4) and ends with "First, choose a quiet place" (2).

questions.question: Which sentence should come FIRST? (1) Farmers welcomed the rain. (2) After weeks of dry weather, rain finally fell over the town. (3) The fields, cracked by the heat, slowly softened. (4) Within days, seedlings began to grow.
questions.explanation: Sentence (2) sets the scene (weeks of dry weather, then rain) and must come first; the rest describe consequences.

questions.question: Which sentence should come LAST? (1) The library opens at 8:00 in the morning. (2) Students borrow books for their lessons. (3) Librarians assist visitors in finding references. (4) In short, the library supports learning for the whole community.
questions.explanation: Sentence (4) is a concluding summary ("In short …"), so it belongs last.

questions.question: Which is the best topic sentence for a paragraph about exercise?

options.A: Regular exercise improves health and energy.
options.C: The gym is near my house.

questions.explanation: Only A states the paragraph's general topic (exercise and its benefits). B, C, D are narrow or off-topic details.

questions.question: Which sentence does NOT belong in a paragraph about saving money? (1) Set aside part of your income each payday. (2) Track your expenses in a notebook. (3) Avoid impulse buying. (4) Penguins live in Antarctica.
questions.explanation: Sentences (1)–(3) are all about saving money; (4) about penguins is unrelated, so it does not belong.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
questions.passage: (1) The small community library on Mabini Street opens its doors every morning at eight. (2) Children gather for story hour, students review lessons, and workers borrow books after their shifts. (3) Volunteers sort donations, repair torn pages, and keep the shelves in order. (4) Last year, residents raised funds to add two computers and a reading corner for toddlers. (5) Because of this shared effort, the library has become a place where learning continues long after school hours.

options.A: The library opens at eight in the morning.
options.B: The library serves the whole community through shared effort.

questions.explanation: The passage shows children, students, workers, volunteers, and residents all using and supporting the library — B captures the whole passage. A is a detail; C and D are minor details.

questions.question: According to the passage, volunteers do NOT
questions.passage: (1) The small community library on Mabini Street opens its doors every morning at eight. (2) Children gather for story hour, students review lessons, and workers borrow books after their shifts. (3) Volunteers sort donations, repair torn pages, and keep the shelves in order. (4) Last year, residents raised funds to add two computers and a reading corner for toddlers. (5) Because of this shared effort, the library has become a place where learning continues long after school hours.
questions.explanation: The passage lists sorting donations, repairing pages, and keeping shelves in order; lending money is never mentioned.

questions.question: The phrase "shared effort" in sentence (5) implies that
questions.passage: (1) The small community library on Mabini Street opens its doors every morning at eight. (2) Children gather for story hour, students review lessons, and workers borrow books after their shifts. (3) Volunteers sort donations, repair torn pages, and keep the shelves in order. (4) Last year, residents raised funds to add two computers and a reading corner for toddlers. (5) Because of this shared effort, the library has become a place where learning continues long after school hours.

options.B: only the staff did the work.

questions.explanation: "Shared effort" refers to residents raising funds plus volunteers working — people working together. B, C, D contradict the passage.

questions.question: The best title for the passage is
questions.passage: (1) The small community library on Mabini Street opens its doors every morning at eight. (2) Children gather for story hour, students review lessons, and workers borrow books after their shifts. (3) Volunteers sort donations, repair torn pages, and keep the shelves in order. (4) Last year, residents raised funds to add two computers and a reading corner for toddlers. (5) Because of this shared effort, the library has become a place where learning continues long after school hours.

options.C: A Library Built by Its Community

questions.explanation: The passage is about a community-built library; C is the best title. A is too vague; B and D cover only details.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the passage?
questions.passage: (1) Mangrove forests grow where seawater meets the shore, their roots rising above the mud like stilts. (2) These roots trap sediment, shelter young fish and crabs, and soften the force of waves during storms. (3) When mangroves are cleared for ponds or buildings, nearby coasts lose both food and protection. (4) Several coastal villages have therefore begun replanting mangroves along river mouths and shorelines. (5) Their work is slow, but each surviving seedling restores a small part of the shore's natural defense.

options.C: To explain how fishing boats work
options.D: To explain the benefits of mangroves and of replanting them

questions.explanation: The passage explains what mangroves do and why replanting matters. A, B, C misstate its purpose.

questions.question: Mangrove roots do NOT

(2) These roots trap sediment, shelter young fish and crabs, and soften the force of waves during storms. questions.explanation: Roots trap sediment, shelter young fish, and soften waves; building concrete walls is not mentioned.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
questions.passage: (1) Before every project, the team of five holds a short planning meeting. (2) Each member states one task, one deadline, and one problem that might delay the work. (3) The leader writes these on a board so everyone can see the full plan at a glance. (4) If a problem appears, the team adjusts the schedule the same day instead of waiting for the deadline. (5) This habit has reduced late submissions and made responsibilities clear to all.

options.B: Short planning meetings make work clearer and more on time.

questions.explanation: The passage shows planning meetings producing clear responsibilities and fewer late submissions. A contradicts it; C and D are unsupported.

questions.question: In the planning meeting, each member states
questions.passage: (1) Before every project, the team of five holds a short planning meeting. (2) Each member states one task, one deadline, and one problem that might delay the work. (3) The leader writes these on a board so everyone can see the full plan at a glance. (4) If a problem appears, the team adjusts the schedule the same day instead of waiting for the deadline. options.D: one task, one deadline, and one possible problem.

questions.explanation: Sentence (2) states it directly: one task, one deadline, one possible problem. A, B, C misstate the list.

questions.question: When a problem appears, the team adjusts the schedule
questions.passage: (1) Before every project, the team of five holds a short planning meeting. (2) Each member states one task, one deadline, and one problem that might delay the work. (3) The leader writes these on a board so everyone can see the full plan at a glance. (4) If a problem appears, the team adjusts the schedule the same day instead of waiting for the deadline. options.A: the same day the problem appears.

questions.explanation: Sentence (4) states the team adjusts "the same day." B, C, D contradict it.

questions.passage: (1) Before every project, the team of five holds a short planning meeting. (2) Each member states one task, one deadline, and one problem that might delay the work. questions.explanation: The passage's lesson is that early adjustment prevents late work. A, B, D contradict the passage.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
questions.passage: (1) In many homes, rainwater runs off the roof and is lost to the drain. (2) A simple barrel placed under a downspout can catch this water for cleaning, watering plants, and flushing. (3) Families who use rain barrels report lower water bills and greener gardens during dry weeks. (4) The water must be covered and kept clean so that mosquitoes do not breed in it. (5) With this small care, a roof that once wasted rain becomes a useful source of water.

options.D: Rain barrels turn wasted rain into useful water.

questions.explanation: The passage is about catching roof rain in a barrel and using it. A, B, C are details or contradictions.

questions.question: Rain-barrel water is used for
questions.passage: (1) In many homes, rainwater runs off the roof and is lost to the drain. questions.explanation: Sentence (2) lists exactly: cleaning, watering plants, and flushing. A is unsafe and not stated; C and D are incomplete.

questions.question: Kasingkahulugan ng MAAGAP
questions.explanation: Maagap means quick to act — "mabilis kumilos." A, C, D are opposites.

questions.question: "Ang ___ ng mga mag-aaral ay kahanga-hanga." Piliin ang angkop na salita.
questions.explanation: Only "kasipagan" (diligence) fits "Ang ___ ng mga mag-aaral ay kahanga-hanga." A, B, C produce nonsense or negative meaning.

questions.question: Kasalungat ng MATAPAT
questions.explanation: The antonym of matapat (faithful/honest) is taksil (traitorous). B, C, D are near-synonyms.

questions.question: Alin ang may wastong gamit ng "nang"?
questions.explanation: "Nang mabilis" correctly uses nang before an adverb (mabilis). A/B use ng before an adverb; D uses nang before a noun (kanin), which is wrong.

questions.question: Kasingkahulugan ng PAYAPA
questions.explanation: Payapa means peaceful — "tahimik." A, C, D describe disturbance or violence.

questions.question: Alin ang may wastong gamit ng "kung" at "kong"?
questions.explanation: "Alam kong darating siya" correctly uses kong (ko + ng). A is wrong: it uses kung (if) where kong is needed, it should be "Alam kong darating siya," the same as D; B uses kung where kong is needed; C mixes them incorrectly.

questions.question: Kasalungat ng MASAGANA
questions.explanation: The antonym of masagana (abundant) is salat (lacking). B and C are synonyms or near-synonyms of masagana; D (masaya, happy) is unrelated and is not the opposite of masagana.

questions.question: Piliin ang wastong pangungusap.

options.A: Sila ay pupunta sa palengke kahapon.
options.B: Sila ay pupunta sa palengke bukas kahapon.
options.C: Sila ay pumunta sa palengke kahapon.
options.D: Sila ay pupunta sa palengke kahapon bukas.

questions.explanation: Past-tense "pumunta" matches "kahapon" (yesterday). A, B, D mix future "pupunta" with "kahapon" (and B/D add "bukas" contradictorily).

questions.question: What is 18% of 350?
What is 2/5 + 1/2?
questions.explanation: Common denominator 10: 2/5 = 4/10; 1/2 = 5/10; 4/10 + 5/10 = 9/10. A, C, D do not equal 9/10.

questions.question: What is 450 − 128 − 97?
questions.explanation: 450 − 128 = 322; 322 − 97 = 225. A, B, C are arithmetic slips.

questions.question: What is 12 × 18?
What is 7.5 + 2.35?
questions.explanation: 7.5 + 2.35 = 9.85 (align decimals: 7.50 + 2.35). A, B, D misalign decimals.

questions.question: What is 5² + 3³?
questions.explanation: 5² = 25; 3³ = 27; 25 + 27 = 52. B, C, D miscalculate a power or the sum.

questions.question: Two amounts are in the ratio 2:3 and their total is 50. What is the smaller amount?
questions.explanation: Ratio parts: 2 + 3 = 5 parts; each part = 50 ÷ 5 = 10; smaller = 2 × 10 = 20. A, B, C use the wrong part or total.

questions.question: An item priced at ₱850 is sold at a 20% discount. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: Discount = 20% × 850 = 170; sale price = 850 − 170 = 680. A, C, D use the wrong discount.

questions.question: What is the average of 12, 18, 22, and 28?
questions.explanation: Sum = 12 + 18 + 22 + 28 = 80; average = 80 ÷ 4 = 20. B, C, D divide or add incorrectly.

questions.question: A bus travels at 45 km/h for 3 hours. How far does it travel?
questions.explanation: Distance = speed × time = 45 × 3 = 135 km. A (120) and C/D miscalculate the product.

questions.question: What is 1/2 of 3/4?
questions.explanation: 1/2 × 3/4 = 3/8. A, B, C are not the product.

questions.question: What is the perimeter of a rectangle 12 m long and 7 m wide?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 2 × (12 + 7) = 2 × 19 = 38 m. A (84) is the area; C and D are half-perimeter errors.

questions.question: What is 0.6 × 40?
questions.explanation: 0.6 × 40 = 24.0. A, B, D misplace the decimal point.

questions.question: What is 144 ÷ 12 + 5?
questions.explanation: Division first: 144 ÷ 12 = 12; 12 + 5 = 17. B ignores +5; C/D add before dividing.

questions.question: If 8 workers can finish a job in 6 days, how many days will 12 workers need at the same rate?
questions.explanation: Inverse proportion: total work = 8 × 6 = 48 worker-days; 48 ÷ 12 workers = 4 days. A, B, C treat it as direct proportion.

questions.question: A tray has 3 dozen eggs. If each egg costs ₱5, what is the total cost?
questions.explanation: 3 dozen = 3 × 12 = 36 eggs; 36 × ₱5 = ₱180. A, C, D use the wrong egg count or price.

questions.question: What is the next number in the sequence 3, 7, 11, 15, …?
questions.explanation: Differences are +4 each time: 3, 7, 11, 15, so next = 15 + 4 = 19. A, B, D break the +4 pattern.

questions.question: How many milliliters are in 2.5 liters?
questions.explanation: 1 L = 1,000 mL, so 2.5 × 1,000 = 2,500 mL. B, C, D misplace zeros.

questions.question: What is the simple interest on ₱4,000 at 5% per year for 2 years?
questions.explanation: Simple interest = P × r × t = 4,000 × 0.05 × 2 = 200 × 2 = ₱400. A is one year only; B, C are wrong products.

questions.question: If 3 is to 5 as x is to 25, what is x?
questions.explanation: 3/5 = x/25 → x = 25 × 3 ÷ 5 = 75 ÷ 5 = 15. A, C, D do not satisfy the proportion.

questions.question: What is the area of a square with a side of 9 m?
questions.explanation: Area = side² = 9² = 81 sq m. A (36) is the perimeter; B, D are wrong products.

questions.question: What is 5! (5 factorial)?
questions.explanation: 5! = 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120. B, C, D are not the full product.

questions.question: What is 20% of 60 plus 30% of 40?
questions.explanation: 20% of 60 = 12; 30% of 40 = 12; 12 + 12 = 24. A, B, C miscalculate a percentage or the sum.

questions.question: Two numbers add up to 48. One number is twice the other. What is the smaller number?
questions.explanation: Let smaller = x, larger = 2x; 3x = 48 → x = 16 (larger 32). A, C, D do not satisfy both conditions.

questions.question: What is the 10th term of the sequence 9, 18, 27, …?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 9: nth term = 9n; 10th = 9 × 10 = 90. A, B, D are not 9 × 10.

questions.question: How many grams are in 0.75 kg?
questions.explanation: 1 kg = 1,000 g, so 0.75 × 1,000 = 750 g. B, C, D misplace zeros.

questions.question: What is 4.8 ÷ 0.6?
questions.explanation: 4.8 ÷ 0.6 = 48 ÷ 6 = 8 (multiply both by 10). A, B, C misplace the decimal.

questions.question: An item bought for ₱120 is sold for ₱150. What is the profit percentage based on cost?
questions.explanation: Profit = 150 − 120 = 30; profit % = 30 ÷ 120 = 0.25 = 25%. A uses selling price as base; C, D are wrong ratios.

questions.question: What is 2/5 expressed as a percentage?
What is the greatest common factor (GCF) of 18 and 24?
questions.explanation: Divisors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18; of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24; greatest common = 6. B, C, D are common divisors but not the greatest (B is not a divisor of 18).

questions.question: A car travels 120 km in 2 hours and 180 km in the next 3 hours. What is its average speed for the whole trip?
questions.explanation: Total distance = 120 + 180 = 300 km; total time = 2 + 3 = 5 h; average = 300 ÷ 5 = 60 km/h. A, B, C are not total distance ÷ total time.

questions.question: What is 15 − (−7)?
questions.explanation: Subtracting a negative: 15 − (−7) = 15 + 7 = 22. A treats it as 15 − 7; C sign error; D is 15 − 8.

questions.question: What is 1,000 decreased by 25%?
questions.explanation: 25% of 1,000 = 250; 1,000 − 250 = 750. A, B, D subtract the wrong amount.

questions.question: If x + 7 = 19, what is x?
questions.explanation: x = 19 − 7 = 12. B, C, D do not satisfy x + 7 = 19.

questions.question: What is 3/8 of 64?
From 8:15 a.m. to 11:45 a.m., how much time has passed?
questions.explanation: 8:15 → 11:15 = 3 h; 11:15 → 11:45 = 30 min; total 3 h 30 min. A, C, D miscount the minutes.

questions.question: What is 12% of 500?
questions.explanation: 12% of 500 = 0.12 × 500 = 60. A (50) is 10%; B, D are wrong products.

questions.question: What is the next number in the sequence 5, 8, 14, 26, 50, …?
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the previous term minus 2: 5 × 2 − 2 = 8; 8 × 2 − 2 = 14; 14 × 2 − 2 = 26; 26 × 2 − 2 = 50; so the next term is 50 × 2 − 2 = 98. (Check with differences: 3, 6, 12, 24 double each time, so the next difference is 48; 50 + 48 = 98.) B (96) uses minus 4, C (100) forgets the minus 2, and D (74) only adds 24 again.

questions.question: Wolf : Pack :: Fish : ___
questions.explanation: A group of wolves is a pack; a group of fish is a school. A (herd) is for cattle/deer, B (flock) for birds/sheep, D (swarm) for bees/insects.

questions.question: Bee : Honey :: Cow : ___
questions.explanation: A bee produces honey; a cow produces milk. B (grass) is what a cow eats, C/D are body parts/products but not what the cow produces as food in this parallel.

questions.question: Bird : Nest :: Bee : ___
questions.explanation: A bee's home is a hive, as a bird's is a nest. B, C, D are other animals' homes.

questions.question: Study : Knowledge :: Practice : ___
questions.explanation: Study produces knowledge; practice produces skill. B, C, D are related to effort but do not name the outcome practice produces.

questions.question: Hand : Glove :: Foot : ___
questions.explanation: A sock covers a foot, as a glove covers a hand. A, B, C cover other body parts.

questions.question: Nose : Smell :: Tongue : ___
questions.explanation: The tongue is used to taste, as the nose is used to smell. A, C, D are other senses.

questions.question: Author : Book :: Composer : ___
questions.explanation: A composer creates a song, as an author creates a book. B, C, D are other creators' works.

questions.question: Knife : Cut :: Broom : ___
questions.explanation: A broom is used to sweep, as a knife is used to cut. A, B, D are other tools' functions.

questions.question: Begin : End :: Arrive : ___
questions.explanation: Depart is the opposite of arrive, as end is the opposite of begin. A, B, C are not opposites of arrive.

questions.question: Clock : Time :: Thermometer : ___
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature, as a clock measures time. A, C, D are measured by other instruments.

questions.question: All teachers are graduates. Maria is a teacher. Therefore,
questions.explanation: Maria belongs to the group (teachers) that are all graduates, so she is a graduate. B contradicts it; C reverses the statement; D is unsupported.

questions.question: If it rains, the ground gets wet. The ground is wet. What validly follows?

options.C: It may or may not have rained.

questions.explanation: Wet ground could have other causes (e.g., spilled water), so rain cannot be proven. A over-concludes; B contradicts nothing; D contradicts the given fact.

questions.question: No cats are dogs. Some pets are cats. Therefore,
questions.explanation: The pets that are cats are in the "cats" group, none of which are dogs — so some pets are not dogs. A, B, C contradict the premises.

questions.question: All clerks are government employees. Juan is a clerk. Therefore,

options.A: Juan is not a government employee.

questions.explanation: Juan is a clerk, and all clerks are government employees. A and C contradict the premises; D reverses the statement.

questions.question: "The office will close early because a typhoon is coming." The statement assumes that

options.A: a typhoon may affect safety or travel.

questions.explanation: Closing early for a typhoon presumes the typhoon may affect safety/travel. B, C, D are not required by the statement.

questions.question: "Only applicants with complete documents will be processed." The statement assumes that

options.B: incomplete documents will also be processed.
options.C: whether an applicant's documents are complete can be determined.

questions.explanation: The statement works only on the unstated assumption that the completeness of an applicant's documents can be checked and determined; without that, the rule could not be applied at all. A is not assumed (the statement does not say every applicant has complete documents); B contradicts the statement; D contradicts it.

questions.question: "Study regularly to pass the examination." The advice assumes that

options.D: regular study helps a person pass.

questions.explanation: The advice presumes regular study helps passing. A contradicts it; B overstates it (guarantee/perfect); C is not required.

questions.question: Some books are novels. All novels are stories. Therefore,
questions.explanation: The books that are novels are stories (since all novels are stories), so some books are stories. A, C, D over-conclude or contradict.

questions.question: If a file is complete, it will be approved. The file was not approved. Therefore,
questions.explanation: Contrapositive: if complete → approved, then not approved → not complete. B and C contradict the given facts; D misses the valid inference.

questions.question: All roses are flowers. Some flowers are red. Therefore,

options.C: no valid conclusion follows that any rose is red.

questions.explanation: The red flowers could all be non-roses; nothing forces a rose to be red. A and B over-conclude; D reverses the statement.

questions.question: Ana is taller than Ben. Ben is taller than Cora. Who is the shortest?
questions.explanation: Order tallest→shortest: Ana > Ben > Cora, so Cora is shortest. A, B, C contradict the ordering.

questions.question: In a line, Maria is ahead of Jose, Jose is ahead of Pedro, and Pedro is ahead of Liza. Who is second in line?
questions.explanation: Order: Maria (1st), Jose (2nd), Pedro (3rd), Liza (4th). So second is Jose. A, C, D are other positions.

questions.question: In a code, each letter is replaced by its position in the alphabet (A=1, B=2, …, Z=26), so CAT is written 3-1-20. How is DOG written?
questions.explanation: D = 4, O = 15, G = 7 → 4-15-7. B swaps O and G; C and D use wrong numbers.

questions.question: A shop's sales were: Monday ₱120, Tuesday ₱150, Wednesday ₱90, Thursday ₱180. What were the total sales for the four days?
questions.explanation: 120 + 150 + 90 + 180 = 540. A, B, D are addition errors.

questions.question: Using the same sales data (Mon ₱120, Tue ₱150, Wed ₱90, Thu ₱180), which day had the highest sales?
questions.explanation: Thursday's ₱180 is the largest (vs. 120, 150, 90). A, B, C are smaller values.

questions.question: Using the same sales data, what was the average daily sales over the four days?
questions.explanation: Average = total ÷ 4 = 540 ÷ 4 = 135. A, C, D are not 540 ÷ 4.

questions.question: What is the next number in the pattern 5, 10, 20, 40, …?
questions.explanation: Each term doubles: 5, 10, 20, 40, so next = 80. B, C, D break the doubling pattern.

questions.question: If today is Wednesday, what day will it be 10 days from now?
questions.explanation: 10 days = 7 days (back to Wednesday) + 3 days → Thursday, Friday, Saturday. So Saturday. A, B, D miscount.

questions.question: A is older than B. B is older than C. C is older than D. Who is the youngest?
questions.explanation: Order oldest→youngest: A > B > C > D, so D is youngest. A, B, C are older.

questions.question: Three departments have 20, 30, and 50 employees. What percentage of all employees are in the 50-employee department?
questions.explanation: Total = 20 + 30 + 50 = 100; 50 ÷ 100 = 50%. A, C, D are other departments' shares.

questions.question: The Philippines is a
questions.explanation: Article II, Section 1 of the 1987 Constitution: the Philippines is a democratic and republican State. B, C, D contradict it.

questions.question: The Executive Department is covered by which Article of the 1987 Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Executive Department is Article VII of the 1987 Constitution. A (Article VI) is the Legislative Department; C (Article VIII) is the Judicial Department; D (Article IX) covers the Constitutional Commissions.

questions.question: Republic Act No. 6713 is the

options.B: Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees.

questions.explanation: RA 6713 is the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees. A is the Local Government Code (RA 7160); C is the civil service law framework; D is RA 3019.

questions.question: Under RA 6713, public officials and employees are required to file a

options.D: Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN).

questions.explanation: Section 8 of RA 6713 requires all public officials and employees to file a Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN), a sworn declaration of what they own, what they owe, and their resulting net worth. The filing is annual: a SALN is filed upon assumption of office and again on or before April 30 of every year thereafter (and within 30 days after separation from service). A, B, C are not the required filing.

questions.question: What is the minimum age for voting (suffrage) in the Philippines?
questions.explanation: Article V, Section 1 of the 1987 Constitution provides that suffrage may be exercised by all citizens of the Philippines, not otherwise disqualified by law, who are at least 18 years of age and who have resided in the Philippines for at least one year and in the place where they propose to vote for at least six months immediately preceding the election. The same section bars any literacy, property, or other substantive requirement for voting. B, C, D are not the constitutional minimum.

questions.question: Legislative power in the Philippines is vested in
questions.explanation: Legislative power is vested in the Congress (Senate + House). A holds executive power; B/D hold judicial/oversight functions.

questions.question: What is the term of office of the President of the Philippines?
questions.explanation: Under Article VII, Section 4 of the 1987 Constitution, the President serves a single term of six years and is not eligible for any reelection, so a former President can never run for the presidency again. For comparison, the three-year term in option D belongs to members of the House of Representatives and to local elective officials, while the four-year and five-year lengths in options A and C are not the term of any Philippine national elective office under the 1987 Constitution.

questions.question: Judicial power is exercised principally by the

options.D: Supreme Court and the lower courts.

questions.explanation: Judicial power is vested in the Supreme Court and the lower courts. A is legislative; B is executive; C is one chamber of Congress.

questions.question: The national language of the Philippines is
questions.explanation: The national language is Filipino. B is an official language for communication/instruction but is not the national language; C and D are not the national language.

questions.question: Which of the following is a norm of conduct under RA 6713?
questions.explanation: Commitment to public interest is a norm of conduct under RA 6713. A, B, D are prohibited/contrary conduct.

questions.question: The Commission on Human Rights (CHR) is a/an
questions.explanation: The CHR is an independent constitutional office under Article XIII of the 1987 Constitution. It is not a court (A), an executive department (C), or a local office (D).

questions.question: Republic Act No. 9147 is the

options.A: Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act.

questions.explanation: RA 9147 is the Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act. B is RA 8749; C is RA 9275; D is RA 9003.

questions.question: Republic Act No. 8749 is the
questions.explanation: RA 8749 is the Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999. B is RA 9275; C is RA 9003; D is RA 9147.

questions.question: Republic Act No. 9275 is the
questions.explanation: RA 9275 is the Philippine Clean Water Act of 2004. A is RA 8749; B is RA 9003; D is RA 9513.

questions.question: The Climate Change Act of 2009 is Republic Act No.
questions.explanation: The Climate Change Act of 2009 is RA 9729. A, C, D are the solid-waste, clean-air, and clean-water acts respectively.

questions.question: Which department is primarily responsible for the country's environment and natural resources?

options.C: Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG)
options.D: Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR)

questions.explanation: The DENR is primarily responsible for the conservation, management, development, and proper use of the country's environment and natural resources. The other departments have different mandates: the DOH (A) handles public health and the national health system, the DepEd (B) handles basic education (elementary and secondary schooling), and the DILG (C) supervises local government units and oversees local governance and peace and order at the local level.

questions.question: Under the 1987 Constitution, the Philippines

options.A: renounces war as an instrument of national policy.
options.B: promotes war as an instrument of national policy.

questions.explanation: Article II, Section 2: the Philippines renounces war as an instrument of national policy. B, C, D contradict the Constitution.

questions.question: The right to due process is guaranteed in the
questions.explanation: Due process is guaranteed in the Bill of Rights (Article III). A, B, D are other articles.

questions.question: The Office of the Ombudsman primarily

options.B: investigates complaints against public officials and acts against graft.

questions.explanation: The Ombudsman investigates complaints against public officials and acts against graft. A is Congress's role; C is the BIR's; D is the President's as commander-in-chief.

questions.question: Freedom of speech in the Philippines is guaranteed by the
questions.explanation: Freedom of speech is guaranteed by the 1987 Constitution (Bill of Rights). A, B, C are statutes that do not themselves grant the right.

questions.question: The Civil Service Commission is a/an
questions.explanation: The Civil Service Commission is an independent constitutional commission created under Article IX of the 1987 Constitution (its own part, Article IX-B, covers the CSC specifically). It is one of the three independent Constitutional Commissions, sitting alongside the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) and the Commission on Audit (COA); these commissions are independent of the executive, legislative, and judicial branches, which is why B, C, and D misstate its character.

questions.question: Appointments in the civil service are based on
questions.explanation: Civil service appointments are based on merit and fitness. A, B, D contradict the merit principle.

questions.question: Under RA 6713, the norm of conduct that requires public officials and employees to perform their duties with the highest degree of excellence, professionalism, intelligence, and skill is called
questions.explanation: Professionalism is the RA 6713 norm requiring duties to be performed with the highest degree of excellence, professionalism, intelligence, and skill. B, C, D are separate norms of conduct under RA 6713.

questions.question: The three stars on the Philippine flag represent
questions.explanation: The three stars stand for the country's three major island groups: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. The flag's other main symbol, the golden sun, has eight rays representing the eight provinces (Manila, Cavite, Bulacan, Pampanga, Nueva Ecija, Tarlac, Batangas, and Laguna) that first rose in revolt against Spain in 1896 and were placed under martial law by the Spanish colonial government. A, B, C are not what the stars represent.

questions.question: Philippine Independence Day is celebrated on
questions.explanation: Independence Day is June 12 (1898 Proclamation). B is a former date; C and D are other holidays.

questions.question: The Philippine national anthem is
questions.explanation: The national anthem is "Lupang Hinirang." A, B, D are other patriotic songs, not the anthem.

questions.question: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the United Nations in
questions.explanation: The UDHR was adopted in 1948. A is the year the UN was founded; C, D are later years.

questions.question: Which of the following is a human right?
questions.explanation: Education is a recognized human right. A, B, C describe wrongdoing, not rights.

questions.question: The 1987 Constitution states that the Philippines pursues a policy of

options.A: peace, equality, justice, freedom, cooperation, and amity with all nations.

questions.explanation: Article II, Section 7: the State pursues an independent foreign policy based on peace, equality, justice, freedom, cooperation, and amity with all nations. B, C, D contradict it.

questions.question: Which practice helps protect the environment?
questions.explanation: Segregating waste supports proper waste management and environmental protection. A, B, D harm the environment. ---
